title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (TIPS 1-10Y, $750M cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding). THE DOCUMENT WAS REISSUED AND RE-READ 2026-09-15: the masthead now reads 'For Publication September 9, 2026' (plain curl, HTTP 200, 89,250 bytes, md5 c49a5351bf2d31a367817abc62be51bd, text layer independently decompressed and re-laid-out by coordinate this session), superseding the 'For Publication August 5, 2026' edition read on 09-03/09-05/09-06/09-08 at 125,547 bytes / md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35. This is sb0607's promised replacement schedule, and the row for this event is VERBATIM UNCHANGED across it: announce 9/28/2026, operation 9/29/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/30/2026, Liquidity Support, TIPS 1Y to 10Y, maturity range 09/30/2027 - 09/29/2036, min $0, max $750 million. What the reissue did move is the nominal long end - the 9/10 10Y-20Y cap reads $6 billion (up from $2 billion, a tripling past sb0607's 'at least double') and the 9/24, 10/1, 10/8, 10/15, 10/27 and 11/4 nominal rows now read '= or > $4 billion' - so TIPS capacity is confirmed flat while nominal long capacity roughly tripled in-quarter. Estimate, not confirmed, on the two counts every buyback row off this document carries: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 09-28 operation announcement rather than this document. Re-checked 2026-09-15
notes: CANONICAL FILE written 2026-09-08 during this event's own initial research, from the one proposal that existed for the id (from-treasury-buyback-tips-10y30y-2026-09-15, filed the same day); that proposal's read is upheld and sharpened. THE FINDING THAT MAKES IT WORTH TRACKING, off api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations (all 220 operations, both pages, fetched 2026-09-08): this is the ONLY TIPS bucket in the program whose cap actually binds — 7 of 8 operations filled 98-100% of the $750M cap, a 93.7% mean fill that ranks 4th of the program's 15 bucket/type categories, against 22.5% (0 of 4) for its TIPS 10Y-30Y sibling and 10.3% (0 of 9) for the 7Y-10Y nominal bucket. The streak broke on 2026-07-22: $405M accepted, a 54.0% fill, on $3,194M offered (12.7% take share). That is the program's ONLY uncensored measurement of this bucket's price-acceptable supply — the other seven are censored at the cap — and it reads BELOW the cap. The mechanism is measurable rather than inferred: total par offered has fallen $6,512M -> $3,194M (-51%) across the eight operations while the maturity window's front rolled a full year (2026-10-15 -> 2027-10-15) and the count of eligible sub-1%-coupon lines fell 14 -> 10. Structurally this is also the only buyback bucket that mixes all four TIPS tenors ever issued: its 27-line July list spans original 30-Year TIPS auctioned 1998-04-08 and 1999-04-07, 20-Year TIPS from 2008/2009, negative-real-yield 10-Year TIPS from 2020-2022, and 5-Year TIPS from 2024/2025 — 27 years of issuance vintage, the exact inverse of the 10Y-30Y bucket, which contains only 30-year paper. Two schedule firsts: 09-29 settles 09/30/2026, the last business day of September AND of Q3 (no prior operation in this bucket settled on a month-end business day), and the August-refunding schedule gives this bucket two rows ($750M each, 9/29 and 10/21) against one $500M TIPS 10Y-30Y row. sb0607 (fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200) names 'nominal coupon securities' only, so this $750M cap is untouched inside the 09-09 -> 11-04 doubled window. Low impact is honest about size: ~$45B of TIPS issuance is scheduled in the same corridor (09-17 10Y reopening, 10-22 new 5Y), a 60:1 issuance-to-cap ratio. Estimate-labelled; nothing here licenses an entry. PULSE 2026-09-15 (D-14), three updates. (1) The reissued schedule leaves this row verbatim unchanged at $750M while nominal long caps triple - the largest open schedule risk is retired. (2) The sibling TIPS 10Y-30Y label filled its $500M cap for the FIRST time on 2026-09-15 (0/4 -> 1/5, mean fill 22.5% -> 38.0%) on $2,088M offered, 2.03x its own four-operation mean and 1.50x its prior maximum, with its eligible count flat at 16 - a tape-driven offer impulse, not an inventory one, which raises this operation's fill odds while putting the draining-inventory mechanism at real risk. (3) The framing above needs one correction the program itself supplied: on 2026-09-10 the nominal 10Y-20Y bucket ran at a tripled $6B cap and took $5,187M (86.5%), its first non-fill in 26 operations, take share 27.0% -> 49.5% - so every 100% fill in the ranking is cap-censored, and 'the only bucket whose cap binds' is a statement about cap size relative to the offer pool rather than about a bucket-specific price filter. The relative ranking survives: TIPS 1Y-10Y 93.7%, 5th of the 12 categories with n >= 4, against 38.0% for TIPS 10Y-30Y and 10.3% for 7Y-10Y nominals. Leg 11's scale deflator is now stronger, not weaker: the 9/17 10Y TIPS reopening is ANNOUNCED at $19.0B (auctions_query, announcement date 2026-09-10), 25:1 against this $750M cap on that leg alone.
